result:
The final pick, `final.py` (same code as c4), scores **70.92** on the official search split, valid, using **4 of the 24 calls**. The baseline scores about 1.0.

| | search score | local held-out (seeds 101–103, my harness) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 (not called) | 1.0 |
| first champion (c1) | 53.7 | not run |
| final pick (c4) | 70.9 | 72–74x faster than the reference, pairs identical to the reference's |

- **Why it is faster:** the baseline compares every pair of records, which is quadratic. The final code uses a prefix-filter inverted index: it indexes each record only under its rarest tokens and only looks up records of compatible size. It then checks the few remaining candidates exactly with `9*inter >= 4*(n+m)`, which is the same test as the reference's `5*inter >= 4*union`.
- **Approaches:** I built only this one family, in four refinements (c1–c4: integer token ranks, fewer sorts, a shorter index prefix). I did not build a bitmask-and-popcount all-pairs version. It would still be quadratic, so I judged it not worth building.
- **Correctness:** every candidate matched the reference exactly on 310 small edge-case lists and on the harness inputs. c2, c3 and c4 also matched on four skewed shapes (tiny vocabulary, long records, heavy duplication, one-token records). The tiny-vocabulary shape is the weak spot: only about 4x faster than the reference. I don't know whether the hidden inputs look like that.
- **Why I stopped:** the scorer measures about 18.9 ms of CPU for the final pick, and a bare Python startup costs about 14.6 ms of that.

Files are in `eval/loop-bench/runs/r9/sonnet/dedup/`: `final.py`, `log.md`, `harness.py`, `stress.py` and candidates `c1.py` to `c4.py`.
